repo.description:
## Impact

The waiting-webhook endpoint accepts a Send-and-Wait node reference in two forms. It decided which validation to apply before normalising the second form, so a request in that shape was accepted without the signature approvals require. A caller holding an execution's resume token can release an approval intended for someone else; everything downstream then runs under the workflow owner's credentials, which depending on the workflow can reach command execution.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 2.42.1 and 2.41.4. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.
- Avoid using Send-and-Wait nodes that gate high-consequence actions in workflows where an earlier public, unauthenticated trigger node exposes a `resumeToken` to external callers.
- Restrict or disable public webhook and chat trigger endpoints that precede Send-and-Wait approval nodes until the instance is patched.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.
repo.summary: Send-and-Wait HMAC Bypass Allows Unauthenticated Approval of Waiting Executions
